_comment: Source entries the benign corpus is KNOWN to produce against the live nine-feed ruleset,
and the reason each is tolerated (PLAN step 11d, issue #75).
The scheduled feeds workflow fails on any source entry whose (source, sid, label_basis)
triple is not listed here. It does NOT assert the counts: upstream rule text changes daily,
and a tolerated rule that stops firing is an improvement, not a regression — the workflow
prints what no longer fires so this file can be shrunk deliberately.
Adding an entry here is the moment to argue that a label on benign traffic is acceptable.
That argument belongs in a reviewed diff, which is why this is a committed file rather than
a list inside the workflow. An entry with no reason is not an entry.
label_basis is part of the key on purpose. A tolerated rule that starts claiming `direct`
where it claimed `indicator-reference` is asserting that ordinary traffic IS an attack, and
that is a regression even though the sid is unchanged.
measured_note: Both rulesets produced the same 12 labels and the same 21 source entries, with the same
three sids in the same proportions. That stability across a 307-rule difference in the
underlying feeds is why this gate can pin the residue rather than wait for zero.

entries.reason: Structurally broken rule: its destination address is literally 127.0.0.1, so it fires on loopback-bound traffic in any capture. Not a taxonomy problem and not fixable by admission policy — the rule is wrong at the source. Since step 11c it publishes indicator-reference rather than direct, which is the honest claim: the flow reached a flagged address. Upstream fix would remove this entry.

A loose FormBook pcre that matches ordinary HTTP. Correctly labelled `direct` — it does inspect payload — so the defect is the rule's precision, not flabel's provenance. Tolerated because the alternative is excluding a real malware signature on the strength of one benign match.

Directionality loss from HOME_NET: any (issue #77). With no inside/outside distinction the rule matches a flow it was not written for. Tracked separately because the fix is a configuration change with a 61% blast radius across the ruleset, not a per-rule decision.
